grid.origin: row 0 = north edge, same grid as client/habitat.png

encoding.index: species_mix_index.png: the cell's row in mixes (0 = no mix: the client's habitat-class mix). 8-bit grey; with index_bytes 2, RGB with the row = R + 256 G
encoding.density: species_mix_density.png RGB: R tree_density, G shrub_density, multiplier = byte / 100 on the client's per-habitat-class plant count (1.0 = the fixed-mix count; the count still scales with client/canopy.png cover); B carpet_density, the dwarf shrubs' share of the shrub density, laid by the ground layer as a carpet in proportion to the canopy.png shrub cover (0: none). The same bytes as the row's density_bytes [tree, shrub(, carpet)]
encoding.weights: mixes[].tree_bytes and shrub_bytes: [[species id, byte], ...], the species with a non-zero weight in the column order of `species`, each layer summing to 255 (absent: no trees or no shrubs). The client draws a species by walking this list in order, so the order is part of the format
encoding.ground: mixes[].ground_bytes: [[species id, byte], ...] over species.ground (the grasses and forbs, library records of form grass or forb, and the dwarf shrubs of the tile's communities: records whose ground block is woody, moved from the shrubs), summing to 255; from each record's habitat block (classes, floor / mid / steep / north) and ground.density, with GROUND_RULES per rule. The client's grass layer draws a cell's grasses from the grasses' share of it and the forb layer its forbs from the forbs' share
encoding.terrain: mixes[].terrain: the terrain classes (effective elevation band, floor / mid-slope / steep, north) whose cells use the row; a community (communities[], one per source and code: its name, the weights and densities as written, and a note) has one row per distinct terrain response (pipeline species_mix.py TERRAIN), and mixes[].community names it. The bytes are after the terrain factors
encoding.structure: mixes[].shrub_h_m: LANDFIRE EVH's shrub height (m), the median over the row's cells where at least half of them have one (absent: none, or a synthetic EVH); mixes[].herb_cover: [low, high] herbaceous cover fraction from the community's LANDFIRE BpS model description (absent: none given)
encoding.stand_ins: stand_ins[]: {species, drawn, reason, cells}: a species a rule or a community's name gives that has no library record, and the record drawn for it: one that belongs to this tile (recorded near it, or of its region where the records cannot say) and is the same genus, else the same family and growth form (pipeline communities.local_stand_in). missing[]: {species, reason, cells}: one with no such record, left out of its rows (the other species take its share); where a community has nothing else in that layer its cells draw the tile's other communities of the habitat class: communities[].generic names the layers and generic_drawn the weights drawn, while its trees / shrubs keep the weights as written. cells: the 30 m cells whose row would have drawn the species
encoding.recorded: communities[].recorded: {species: {records, of, affinity}}: the shrubs added to the community from the records on its own cells (pipeline/associates.py): open-licence GBIF observations within recorded_associates.buffer_km of the tile laid on LANDFIRE's vegetation map. records: on cells of this community; of: on any natural cell; affinity: its share of records here over all plants' share here (1 = as visits alone would put it; a member has a standard error more than that, associates.excess). They rank after the species LANDFIRE lists, each weighing min(1, records / 30) over its rank, and together weigh no more than those; a thin one's share goes to the listed species. recorded_associates: the records' count, licences and GBIF datasets (the attribution)
encoding.recorded_support: communities[].recorded_support: where no shrub is listed and the records alone give the layer (weights.shrubs = recorded), how much of the habitat class's shrub density they support: the sum over the members of min(1, records on this community's cells / 30) / rank, at most 1. The shrub density and the carpet density (as listed) are already multiplied by it; the rest of the layer is left empty
encoding.held_empty: communities[].held_empty: {layer: share}: the share of the layer's weights on species the client has no growth form for (a cactus, a yucca, an agave without a record: communities.NO_GROWTH_FORM). They are in `missing`; unlike other missing species their share is not given to the community's other species: the layer's density (as listed) is already lower by that share

riparian.encoding: rows[zone|order class|permanence]: trees / shrubs / ground as [[species id, byte]] summing to 255 per layer (absent: none), density [tree, shrub, ground] multipliers; the zone, order (small 1-2, medium 3-4, large 5+) and permanence come from client/water.png R; pond zones use the class 'pond'; a key ending '|<band>' is the row for ground in that elevation band (bands_m: band = how many of its heights the ground is at or above)
